definitions.explanation: The gradual building up of something over time, typically debts, deficits, data, fatigue, or other quantities that keep adding up. Often implies a negative buildup.

examples.japanese: {赤字|あかじ}が{累積|るいせき}している。
{累積|るいせき}{債務|さいむ}が{膨大|ぼうだい}な{額|がく}に{達|たっ}した。
examples.english: The accumulated debt has reached an enormous amount.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{疲労|ひろう}が{累積|るいせき}して{体|からだ}を{壊|こわ}した。
examples.english: Years of accumulated fatigue broke down my body.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used with negative quantities — debts, deficits, losses, fatigue. Also used in neutral/technical contexts like {累積|るいせき}データ (cumulative data) and {累積|るいせき}{販売|はんばい}{数|すう} (cumulative sales figures). Common in finance, business, and statistics.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {蓄積|ちくせき}: accumulation, storage (more positive, for knowledge, experience)
- {集積|しゅうせき}: aggregation, concentration (clustering together)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {累積|るいせき}{赤字|あかじ}: accumulated deficit
- {累積|るいせき}{債務|さいむ}: accumulated debt
- {累積|るいせき}{販売|はんばい}{数|すう}: cumulative sales figures
- {疲労|ひろう}が{累積|るいせき}する: fatigue accumulates
